directions.title: Welded structures
directions.description: Explore how welding affects the stresses and fatigue life of a component. A thesis can connect process simulations with measurements and tests on welded joints.
directions.activities: Welding simulation; thermomechanical finite element models; residual stress evaluation; fatigue testing and numerical–experimental comparison.

directions.title: Multiaxial fatigue of metals
directions.description: Study how metals accumulate fatigue damage when loads act in several directions. Develop and compare assessment methods, with opportunities for students interested in mechanics, programming and scientific computing.
directions.activities: Critical-plane criteria; efficient algorithms; model benchmarking; validation against experimental datasets; Python-based scientific software.

directions.title: Fatigue behaviour of polymers
directions.description: Investigate how polymeric materials behave under repeated loading and how to predict the life of polymer components. The balance between testing and modelling can follow your interests and the agreed project.
directions.activities: Mechanical and cyclic characterisation; constitutive and fatigue-life models; component simulations; experimental validation. Temperature effects may be considered where feasible.

directions.title: PCB fatigue and reliability
directions.description: Explore the mechanical reliability of printed circuit boards and electronic assemblies. Potential applications include components exposed to cyclic or vibration loading in automotive and other engineering environments.
directions.activities: Finite element models of boards and components; mechanical response and failure mechanisms; fatigue-life estimation; comparison with measurements.

directions.title: AI for structural integrity
directions.description: Explore whether data-driven methods can support fatigue prediction and structural assessment. Specific AI projects depend on suitable datasets, research collaborators and agreed thesis objectives; these are potential directions, not claims of established or validated tools.
directions.activities: Machine-learning benchmarks; physics-based and data-driven models; surrogate modelling; interpretation of experimental data against reference results.

approaches.title: Numerical / computational
approaches.description: Finite element simulations, analytical methods, programming and algorithm development. Compare models and check their predictions against reference data.

approaches.title: Experimental
approaches.description: Laboratory testing, specimen characterisation, measurements and data acquisition. Interpret results to understand material and component behaviour.

approaches.title: Combined
approaches.description: Build a numerical model and support it with experiments. Correlate simulations with measurements and validate structural or fatigue assessment methods.
